description: Common biological mathematical modelling parameters, compiled from retrieved BioModels, Europe PMC, Reactome, SBML and classic model sources.

sources.name: Hodgkin and Huxley action potential model
Kermack and McKendrick compartmental epidemic model
Chen et al. ErbB signaling mass-action model
Konig et al. human hepatic glucose metabolism model

entries.definition: Substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half of Vmax under a Michaelis-Menten rate law.

typical_values.context: typically reported in kinetic tables or fitted parameter sets

entries.definition: Asymptotic reaction velocity approached as substrate concentration becomes saturating in a Michaelis-Menten model.

typical_values.context: reported with enzyme amount or normalized to protein concentration

entries.definition: Number of substrate molecules converted per enzyme active site per unit time under saturating substrate conditions.

typical_values.context: often derived as Vmax divided by enzyme concentration

entries.definition: Ratio of catalytic turnover to Michaelis constant, often used as a measure of enzyme efficiency at low substrate concentration.

typical_values.context: high values indicate efficient catalysis at low substrate

entries.definition: Second-order rate constant governing formation of a complex from its binding partners.

typical_values.context: used in mass-action binding and receptor-ligand kinetics

entries.definition: First-order rate constant governing dissociation of a bound complex.

typical_values.context: used with kon to determine equilibrium binding affinity

entries.definition: Equilibrium ratio koff/kon for a reversible binding reaction; lower values indicate tighter binding.

typical_values.context: used for receptor-ligand or protein-complex affinity

entries.definition: Dissociation constant for inhibitor binding to free enzyme or enzyme-substrate complex in inhibition models.

typical_values.context: used in competitive, noncompetitive, and uncompetitive inhibition expressions

entries.definition: Concentration of an inhibitor producing 50% reduction of a specified response under stated assay conditions.

typical_values.context: requires assay, substrate, time, and endpoint context

entries.definition: Concentration producing 50% of the maximal observed effect under stated experimental conditions.

typical_values.context: requires response definition and assay context

entries.definition: Empirical exponent in a Hill function that describes cooperativity or apparent ultrasensitivity.

typical_values.context: n=1 is noncooperative; larger values indicate steeper response

entries.definition: Context-dependent rate parameter for transmission in epidemic models or production in gene-expression models.

typical_values.context: must be interpreted from the enclosing model

entries.notes: Symbol beta is used in multiple model families; semantic review must retain context-specific disambiguation.

entries.definition: Rate at which infected individuals recover or leave the infectious compartment in SIR/SEIR models.

typical_values.context: inverse gives mean infectious period

entries.definition: Rate of transition from exposed to infectious compartment in SEIR-type models.

typical_values.context: inverse gives mean latent period

entries.definition: Expected number of secondary infections generated by one infected individual in a fully susceptible population.

typical_values.context: for simple SIR, R0=beta/gamma

entries.definition: Per-capita rate of increase in population size, tumor volume, or biomass.

typical_values.context: used in exponential, logistic, and Gompertz models

entries.definition: Maximum population size supported by the environment in logistic and related growth models.

typical_values.context: must be distinguished from equilibrium constants symbolized by K

entries.notes: Symbol K is highly context-dependent; keep separate from Km, Kd, and inhibition constants.

entries.definition: Rate constant or volume-normalized rate describing removal of a substance from a compartment.

typical_values.context: used in one-compartment and biomarker kinetic models

entries.definition: Rate parameter describing entry or release of a substance into a measured compartment.

typical_values.context: paired with clearance in input-output kinetic models

entries.definition: Time required for a quantity to fall to half of its reference value under a specified kinetic process.

typical_values.context: for first-order decay, t_half=ln(2)/k

entries.definition: Proportionality constant relating diffusive flux to a concentration gradient under Fickian transport.

typical_values.context: used in reaction-diffusion models

entries.definition: Electrical potential difference across a cell membrane.

typical_values.context: central state variable in Hodgkin-Huxley models

entries.definition: Maximum ionic conductance associated with a channel population in electrophysiological models.

typical_values.context: multiplied by gating variables in Hodgkin-Huxley currents

entries.definition: Membrane potential at which net ionic current for a given ion reverses direction.

typical_values.context: used in driving-force terms (Vm-Eion)

entries.definition: Capacitance per unit membrane area relating charge accumulation to membrane potential.

typical_values.value: commonly about 1 µF/cm^2 in many preparations
typical_values.context: membrane equation Cm dV/dt = -I_total

entries.definition: Rate parameter controlling production of mRNA in gene-expression models.

typical_values.context: observed in the repressilator SBML model as alpha, alpha0, a_tr, and a0_tr

entries.definition: First-order removal rate for mRNA in gene-expression models.

typical_values.context: observed in BIOMD0000000012 repressilator model

entries.definition: First-order removal rate for protein in gene-expression models.

typical_values.context: observed in BIOMD0000000012 repressilator model

entries.definition: Rate parameter controlling protein production from mRNA.

typical_values.context: observed in BIOMD0000000012 repressilator model

entries.definition: Characteristic time scale for mRNA turnover, often reciprocal of mRNA degradation rate.

typical_values.context: observed in BIOMD0000000012 repressilator model

entries.definition: Characteristic time scale for protein turnover, often reciprocal of protein degradation rate.

typical_values.context: observed in BIOMD0000000012 repressilator model

entries.definition: Concentration of catalytically active enzyme available to convert substrate to product.

typical_values.context: used to convert Vmax to kcat

entries.definition: Concentration of substrate available for an enzymatic or transport reaction.

typical_values.context: input to saturation and inhibition expressions

entries.definition: Concentration of product generated by a reaction or transported across a compartment.

typical_values.context: state variable in kinetic networks

entries.definition: Rate of conversion through a reaction or pathway under a specified kinetic law.

typical_values.context: may be simulated, measured, or constrained

entries.definition: Local sensitivity of reaction rate to a metabolite concentration in metabolic control analysis.

typical_values.context: observed in linlog metabolic models

entries.definition: Change in Gibbs free energy associated with a reaction or transition.

typical_values.context: sign indicates favorable or unfavorable direction

entries.definition: Probability associated with binding, occupancy, or transition between discrete states.

typical_values.context: must be distinguished from p-values and generic probability notation

entries.definition: Concentration assigned at the start of a simulation or observation window.

typical_values.context: reported in initial-condition sections or parameter tables

entries.definition: Thermodynamic temperature affecting kinetic constants, diffusion, and conformational transitions.

typical_values.context: often introduced through Arrhenius or Q10 relationships

entries.definition: Relative change in a steady-state pathway flux caused by a relative change in an enzyme activity or reaction rate.

typical_values.context: summation theorem in metabolic control analysis

entries.notes: Central quantity in metabolic control analysis; distinct from concentration control coefficients.

entries.definition: Relative change in a steady-state metabolite concentration caused by a relative change in an enzyme activity or reaction rate.

typical_values.value: sum to zero across a pathway
typical_values.context: summation theorem in metabolic control analysis

entries.notes: Sign indicates whether a metabolite rises or falls with increasing enzyme activity.

entries.definition: Relative change in a system variable caused by a relative change in an external parameter or effector.

typical_values.context: links external effectors to pathway responses

entries.notes: Symbol R is also used for reproduction number and rates; requires context disambiguation.

entries.definition: Ratio of product activities to reactant activities at prevailing concentrations, used to assess displacement from equilibrium.

typical_values.context: thermodynamic feasibility analysis

entries.notes: Distinguish from the reaction quotient symbol Q used elsewhere.

entries.definition: Ratio of product to reactant activities at thermodynamic equilibrium for a reaction.

typical_values.context: relates to standard free energy by Keq = exp(-DeltaG0/RT)

entries.notes: Symbol K overlaps with Km and carrying capacity; keep separate with disambiguation.

symbol_conflicts.resolution: PARAM_KCAT uses kcat alone; PARAM_KCAT_KM is the composite efficiency ratio.
E denotes enzyme concentration only in enzyme-kinetics context; E_Na, E_K, and E_L denote reversal potentials in electrophysiology.
Duplicate spelling within one entry was normalized; canonical symbol is k_tl.
P denotes product concentration in reaction kinetics and a probability in stochastic or state models; context determines the meaning.
